The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy warship, and ignited a fire at the naval base, they said. Several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship from a base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya, according to an initial investigation into the attack. Sports.title: Kildunne returns to haunt Harlequins as Bristol get PWR season off to a flyer
Sports.summary: Harlequins 21-48 Bristol Full-back marks debut with two tries against former club As women’s rugby grows, more scrutiny will follow and Ellie Kildunne has felt that over the past few months. Her performances have been put under a microscope after being dropped to the bench in England’s final two WXV matches in October , but she silenced her critics with a stellar and trademark performance in her club debut for Bristol. The full-back did it under significant pressure, too, as she returned to the Stoop five months after her shock exit from Harlequins and helped Bristol beat her former side in their Premiership Women’s Rugby opener. The Bristol head coach, Scott Lawson, had thrown his full backing behind Kildunne in the buildup, saying that being at the West Country club would “bring the best” out of the 27-year-old and if her debut is anything to go by he will be proved right. The World Cup winner not only scored two tries but was also a linchpin in Bristol’s attack. Her attacking prowess and gamechanging reputation was felt among her former teammates as she drew multiple players to her whenever she had the ball, meaning the wings on her outside had a lot more joy. The back three looked formidable with both wings, Reneeqa Bonner and Millie David, also scoring two tries apiece. Continue reading...

Culture.title: Hark! Errollyn Wallen’s glittering nativity opera A Christmas Miracle is a credit to Britten’s community vision
Culture.summary: Orford church, Suffolk Performed in the venue where Noye’s Fludde premiered and based on the same text, this festive new work shines with exuberant young performers, distinctive singalongs, lustrous designs and the spirit of mucking in When Benjamin Britten wrote Noye’s Fludde, he essentially invented community opera. Bringing professionals together with enthusiastic local amateurs, everyone mucking in to play, sing and make sets and costumes, isn’t only great fun; done right, it fosters a love of music-making that can last a lifetime. Such projects, the composer declared with his best socialist hat on, created works that were “useful to the living”. For decades, Britten contemplated a nativity opera, which somehow never transpired. Now, Errollyn Wallen , Master of the King’s Music, has filled the gap. A Christmas Miracle, co-produced by Mahogany Opera and Britten Pears Arts, sets texts from the same Chester mystery plays that inspired Noye’s Fludde, and premiered in the Orford church that Britten chose in 1958. Culture.title: Interpol and Bloc Party review – two of 00s indie’s most revered acts go toe-to-toe
Culture.summary: Utilita Arena Cardiff Kele Okereke has a tough challenge selling Bloc Party’s trite latest album – a far cry from Interpol’s ‘masterpiece’ eighth record, performed here to darkly hypnotic effect Try as one might to resist comparison, the balance of this particular yin and yang has been shifting for some time. Twelve months ago, when Interpol and Bloc Party announced a UK and European co-headline tour, the pairing looked like an even contest: two of 00s indie’s most revered acts, whose landmark debuts remain touchstones of the era. Since then, their fortunes have diverged. As an opening bass drone strafes the room, Bloc Party arrive in Cardiff in superficially fine, if puzzling, form. Their seventh album, Anatomy of a Brief Romance, has been met with diminishing returns, its Snapchat-caption triteness – “Every day is such a vibe”, runs one refrain – and creative inertia doing little to win over listeners.
